newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso budget offers help with farm inputs.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso budget offers help with farm inputs.

text.p: Burkina Faso's government has submitted a draft 1997 budget to parliament with a lower deficit than in 1996 and a special contribution to help farmers buy fertiliser and pesticides.
The budget draft projects spending of 397.43 billion CFA francs, up 10.2 percent on 1996.
With projected government revenue up 15.5 percent, the projected deficit falls from 38.9 billion CFA to 25.58 billion CFA, or 1.86 percent of gross domestic product.
Officials said that the government aimed to plug the gap by improving collection of taxes, curbing spending and with the help of the West African nation's development partners.
The draft includes a special allocation of 1.2 billion CFA to help with farm inputs.
Burkina Faso has a programme to boost farm production with the aim of self-sufficiency. Cereal production this year notched up a surplus.
Insect damage cut this year's output of cotton, a major export, to 180,000 tonnes from an expected 200,000 tonnes.
The budget debate was expected to last all week.
